entries.why: A written statement of browser expectations is a document a person must supply; no check reads documentation.
Whether a resource can be framed or rendered out of context depends on the headers a deployed server really sends; no JGates check inspects that.

checks.covers: Assignments to innerHTML or outerHTML, document.write and insertAdjacentHTML fed a value that is not a literal, in JavaScript and TypeScript.
checks.misses: Other languages, jQuery html(), framework-specific sinks, values wrapped by a sanitizer the rule does not recognize, and any proof that the data was meant to be text.

checks.covers: React markup props that inject a non-literal value as HTML.
checks.misses: Other front-end frameworks, a sanitizer the rule does not know, and any judgment on the data's intent.

checks.covers: A model traces browser-controlled sources into HTML-writing sinks and framework escape hatches.
checks.misses: Anything the model does not read; the finding depends on its source reading only.

entries.why: The rules and the audit block look for the unsafe way of writing text into the page, which is the opposite of the safe rendering the requirement wants.

checks.covers: A model looks for injected id or name attributes that shadow a global or configuration value the code later trusts.
checks.misses: Code outside the reviewed files, and whether the page applies every protective practice the requirement lists.

entries.why: The audit class is the same attack the requirement guards against, so a completed review of it examines part of the requirement.
No check reads cookie attributes or cookie-name prefixes; the audit class on cookies treats missing flags as hardening notes only.
No check looks at the SameSite value chosen for each cookie.
No check looks at cookie-name prefixes.
No check reads the HttpOnly attribute of cookies or how a session value reaches the client.
Cookie size depends on the data a running system stores; a source check cannot bound it.
The header must be present on every response of the deployed system; no JGates check inspects live responses for it.

checks.covers: The Express cors() middleware configured with a wildcard origin and credentials together.
checks.misses: Reflected or weakly matched origins, CORS set by hand on responses, other frameworks and languages, and a wildcard on a response that carries sensitive data without credentials; browsers refuse a bare wildcard on credentialed requests, so a finding shows a wildcard policy on user-bound responses rather than a proven leak.

checks.covers: A model checks whether the server reflects or loosely matches the Origin value while allowing credentials and returning sensitive data.
checks.misses: Behavior of the deployed server and proxies; only the source that was read.

entries.why: The rule catches the worst wildcard setup and the audit block catches origin values accepted without a proper allowlist, which are the two ways the requirement is violated in code.
The policy header is set by the running application or its proxy; no JGates check reads response headers.
Needs the real response headers of a deployed system; no JGates check inspects them.
A referrer policy lives in response headers or page markup of a deployed system; no JGates check inspects either.
The directive must be on every response of the running system; the clickjacking audit class treats missing headers on read-only content as a hardening note, so it does not examine this.
The reporting location is part of a deployed policy header that no JGates check reads.
Needs the headers of live document responses; no JGates check reads them.

checks.covers: Django-style views decorated with csrf_exempt, which removes the token check.
checks.misses: Other Python frameworks, CSRF defenses that are absent rather than disabled, and views protected by another means.

checks.covers: Spring Security configuration that switches CSRF protection off.
checks.misses: Applications where protection was never added, other Java frameworks, and token-authenticated endpoints where disabling is intended.

checks.covers: A model inventories cookie-authenticated mutations and checks whether each has a token, same-site binding or strict origin validation.
checks.misses: Anything outside the source the model read, and endpoints it does not enumerate.

entries.why: Each check examines whether state-changing requests from another site are validated, which is the control the requirement asks for when preflight is not relied on.
No check tests whether sensitive functionality can be called with a request that avoids a preflight.
No check maps sensitive operations to the HTTP method used to reach them.
Which hostnames serve which applications is a deployment fact outside the repository.

checks.covers: A model looks at message handlers that act on event data without an exact origin allowlist.
checks.misses: Syntax validation of the message body is not the focus, and handlers the model does not read are missed.

entries.why: The audit class examines the origin check of message handlers, which is the core of the requirement.
No check looks for JSONP endpoints.
No check looks for authorization-bound data placed in script responses.
Depends on request-header validation or a resource policy header of a deployed system; no JGates check examines either.
No check reads page markup for externally hosted assets or integrity attributes; the supply-chain method concerns dependencies and releases, not this.
No check identifies obsolete browser plugin technologies.

checks.covers: A model checks browser-side code where a source controls a redirect or navigation without destination policy.
checks.misses: Server-side redirects in HTTP responses, which the requirement also covers, are not part of this block.

entries.why: The audit class looks for redirects steered by input without a destination policy, which is half of what the requirement concerns (the browser side).
No check looks for an interstitial before leaving the application.
Membership of a public preload list is an external fact about a domain, not visible in the repository.
Needs observation of the application in browsers lacking the features, plus the document that states the intended behavior.
